# Part A-Creating Vectors
```{r}

scores <- c(88, 92, 79, 95, 84)
subjects <- c("Math", "Science", "English", "History", "PE")
odds <- seq(1,19, by = 2)
seq(0,1, length.out = 5)

rep("A", 4)
rep(c("A","B"), each = 2)
rep(c("A", "B"), times = 2)

age <- c (15, 28, 32, 36, 27, 18, 52, 39, 42, 29, 35, 31, 27, 22, 37, 34, 19, 20, 57, 49, 50, 37, 46, 25, 17, 12, 42, 53, 41, 51, 35, 24, 33, 8)
length(age)
1 / age
new_age <- c(age, 0, age)
length(new_age)
min(age)
max(age)

Question 1:
a.How many data points?
b.Find the reciprocal of age?
  The reciprocal of age is calculated 1 by each element in the vector
c.Assign also new_age <- c(age, 0, age). What happens to new_age?
  It conatins 69 elements.
d.Find the minimum and the maximum value of age.
  The minimum value of age is 8 and the maximum value is 57.
  
Question 2:

-rep(c("A","B"), each = 2) and rep(c("A","B"), times = 2) both produce a vector of length 4, but with different element orders.
  The each arguments repeats every element the specified number of times producing "A" "A" "B" "B". In contrast, timmes repeats the entire vector, producing "A" "B" "A" "B".
  

  

  



```
